ABOUT THE CLIENT

chunks.page_title: Cement ESG & Sustainability Portal | Case Study | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: A multi-state cement enterprise managing sustainability performance across a large industrial footprint.
heading_path: A multi-state cement enterprise managing sustainability performance across a large industrial footprint.
chunks.content:
The client is a leading India-based cement manufacturer operating more than thirty plants with combined production capacity exceeding sixty million tonnes per annum. Sustainability performance is monitored across plant operations, energy, environment, production, finance and corporate ESG functions.
The operating environment generates high-frequency information from meters, production systems, laboratories, ERP platforms, environmental monitoring systems and manually maintained records. More than a dozen sustainability and operational parameters are captured, with selected data available at hourly frequency.
02
THE CHALLENGE

chunks.page_title: Cement ESG & Sustainability Portal | Case Study | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Sustainability data existed everywhereâbut not as one dependable management picture.
heading_path: Sustainability data existed everywhereâbut not as one dependable management picture.
chunks.content:
Environmental and operational information was spread across Excel files, paper registers, emails, departmental systems, manual meter readings, utility bills, laboratory records and ERP reports. Consolidating this information across plants was slow, difficult to validate and heavily dependent on manual intervention.
Carbon accounting required repeated calculations across fuels, electricity and other activity data. Plant comparisons, target-versus-actual monitoring, regulatory reporting and management analysis were delayed, while fragmented evidence and correction processes made auditability difficult.
No consolidated ESG view
Carbon, energy, water, waste and environmental metrics were distributed across plants and systems.
Manual carbon accounting
Scope 1 and Scope 2 calculations depended on repeated consolidation and emission-factor application.
Limited plant comparison
Management could not consistently compare intensity, efficiency and target performance across sites.
Reporting and audit effort
Regulatory and sustainability reporting required extensive validation, evidence gathering and reconciliation.
03
THE SOLUTION

chunks.page_title: Cement ESG & Sustainability Portal | Case Study | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: One governed sustainability operating layer from plant data to board-level insight.
heading_path: One governed sustainability operating layer from plant data to board-level insight.
chunks.content:
Eureka designed a connected ESG platform combining Power Pages, ASP.NET, React, Microsoft SQL Server, Power BI, Azure, Power Automate, APIs, IoT integrations and JavaScript visualisation libraries. The platform creates a common sustainability data model across plants while preserving source, approval, evidence and reporting context.

Executive ESG visibility across plants and performance areas
chunks.content: The portal provides executive dashboards covering carbon and GHG emissions, energy consumption, renewable and non-renewable energy, water, waste and hazardous waste, alternative fuels and raw materials, production, clinker and cement metrics, emission intensity, ESG targets, compliance, sustainability initiatives, alerts and plant comparisons.

chunks.page_title: Cement ESG & Sustainability Portal | Case Study | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Scope 1 and Scope 2 carbon accounting with Scope 3 readiness
heading_path: One governed sustainability operating layer from plant data to board-level insight.
Scope 1 and Scope 2 carbon accounting with Scope 3 readiness
chunks.content: The platform calculates direct Scope 1 and energy-indirect Scope 2 emissions using approved emission factors and COâe conversion logic across relevant fuels, electricity and activity data. Carbon intensity can be analysed per tonne of clinker or cement against baseline years and target trajectories. The data model is being extended to support Scope 3 value-chain categories such as transportation and purchased goods.

chunks.page_title: Cement ESG & Sustainability Portal | Case Study | Eureka Solutions
heading_path: One governed sustainability operating layer from plant data to board-level insight.
Energy and plant-efficiency intelligence
chunks.content: Operational analytics include electrical energy per tonne, thermal energy per tonne, renewable-energy share, fuel mix, alternative-fuel substitution, plant efficiency, production-versus-energy relationships, energy cost, trends and benchmarks. This allows sustainability teams to connect environmental outcomes with the operational drivers behind them.

chunks.page_title: Cement ESG & Sustainability Portal | Case Study | Eureka Solutions
heading_path: One governed sustainability operating layer from plant data to board-level insight.
Environmental performance beyond carbon
chunks.content: Water withdrawal, consumption and recycling, particulate matter, NOx, SOx, waste generation, disposal and recycling, biodiversity indicators and raw-material metrics are brought into the same plant-level and enterprise reporting structure.

chunks.page_title: Cement ESG & Sustainability Portal | Case Study | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Governed data from plant entry through consolidated reporting
heading_path: One governed sustainability operating layer from plant data to board-level insight.
Governed data from plant entry through consolidated reporting
chunks.content: Plant users enter or import data, automated validation rules check completeness and consistency, department approvers review submissions, and the ESG team performs consolidated review before calculations and reporting. Maker-checker controls, approval hierarchies, evidence uploads, corrections, audit history and reporting-period locks preserve accountability.

chunks.page_title: Cement ESG & Sustainability Portal | Case Study | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Framework-aligned reporting without disconnecting it from operations
heading_path: One governed sustainability operating layer from plant data to board-level insight.
Framework-aligned reporting without disconnecting it from operations
chunks.content: The platform supports sustainability information mapped to BRSR, the GHG Protocol, CDP, the UN Sustainable Development Goals and internal sustainability targets. Reporting remains linked to the underlying plant and operational data rather than becoming a separate manual reporting exercise.

AI-assisted recommendations help teams identify potential improvement areas across energy, carbon, water, waste utilisation and alternative-fuel use for expert review and prioritisation.

The platform had to balance financial integrity, regulatory readiness, customer accessibility, multi-currency processing, auditability, high availability and future scalability without creating a fragmented multi-vendor technology estate.

chunks.content:
The client is an East Asia-based shipping and logistics company coordinating sea-freight movements across a large international network of customers, shipping lines, agents, freight partners and ports.
Its operating environment covers more than seventy-five countries and over one hundred customers, requiring continuous coordination of bookings, containers, vessels, documents, costs and shipment milestones from origin through final delivery.

THE CHALLENGE

chunks.page_title: Shipping & Freight Planner | Case Study | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Global freight movement was being coordinated through spreadsheets, email and manual follow-up.
heading_path: Global freight movement was being coordinated through spreadsheets, email and manual follow-up.
chunks.content:
Bookings, container records, shipping documents, freight costs and vessel updates were maintained across multiple Excel files and email exchanges with shipping agents. ETA and ETD changes were frequently tracked manually, making it difficult to maintain one dependable operating picture across shipments and customers.
The lack of real-time visibility created operational risk around missed milestones, inaccurate customer updates, route changes, detention and demurrage exposure, and exception management. Teams spent substantial time asking where shipments were rather than acting on the shipments that required attention.
No consolidated freight view
Bookings, containers, documents, costs and milestones were maintained in separate working files.
Manual ETA / ETD tracking
Teams repeatedly checked agents and carriers for schedule updates and delays.
Exception risk
Missed milestones increased exposure to detention, demurrage and service-level failures.
Difficult customer communication
Shipment updates depended on internal teams manually collecting and relaying information.
03

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: Agentic AI Solutions & AI Agents | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Considering where AI agents could create value in your business?
heading_path: Considering where AI agents could create value in your business?
chunks.content:
What is the difference between an AI assistant and an AI agent?
An assistant primarily responds to a user request. An agent can be designed to pursue a defined goal across multiple steps, use approved tools and data, take permitted actions and involve a person when approval or judgment is required.
Does agentic AI mean giving AI full autonomy?
No. Autonomy should match the process and its risk. An agent may act independently on low-risk steps while requiring human approval for sensitive, financial, customer-facing or irreversible actions.
Can AI agents work with our existing ERP, CRM or internal applications?
Yes, where suitable APIs, services, databases or other controlled integration mechanisms are available. We assess each system before defining what information and actions an agent can safely access.
How do you reduce incorrect or inappropriate agent actions?
We combine grounded enterprise context, constrained tools, permissions, validation rules, approval checkpoints, logging and fallback paths. The exact controls depend on the consequence of each action.
Should every automated process use agentic AI?
No. Stable, deterministic processes are often better handled with conventional workflow automation. Agentic AI is most useful where work needs interpretation, contextual reasoning or flexible multi-step coordination.
Can we start with a small proof of concept?
Yes. A focused use case with clear inputs, actions and success criteria is often the right way to validate value, risk controls and integration feasibility before expanding the solution.

chunks.page_title: AI Assistants & Copilots | Enterprise AI Solutions | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning an enterprise AI assistant or role-specific copilot?
heading_path: Planning an enterprise AI assistant or role-specific copilot?
chunks.content:
How is an enterprise AI assistant different from a public AI chatbot?
An enterprise assistant can be designed around approved internal knowledge, user identity, role permissions, business terminology and selected application context rather than relying only on a general-purpose public conversation experience.
Can the assistant answer questions from our internal documents?
Yes. Approved documents and knowledge repositories can be indexed or connected using suitable retrieval methods, with access rules applied according to the source and user requirements.
Can different departments have different copilots?
Yes. Separate or role-aware assistant experiences can be created for functions with different knowledge, terminology, workflows and permissions instead of forcing one universal assistant.
Can an assistant also update our business systems?
Where appropriate, an assistant can initiate or prepare controlled actions through supported APIs and workflows. Sensitive actions can require explicit confirmation or approval before execution.
How do you control access to confidential information?
Access design can combine authenticated identity, role permissions, source-level controls and application security. The architecture should ensure the assistant only retrieves or exposes information the user is permitted to access.
Can we begin with one focused assistant use case?
Yes. Starting with a defined user group, trusted knowledge set and measurable task is often the best way to validate usefulness, response quality and governance before expanding scope.

chunks.page_title: AI Chatbots & Virtual Assistants | Conversational AI | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning a customer or employee virtual assistant?
heading_path: Planning a customer or employee virtual assistant?
chunks.content:
How is an AI chatbot different from a traditional rule-based chatbot?
Traditional bots typically depend on predefined menus, keywords and fixed flows. AI chatbots can interpret natural language and use approved knowledge to handle a wider variety of phrasing, while structured flows can still be retained where predictable control is important.
Can the chatbot answer questions from our own documents and FAQs?
Yes. Approved FAQs, policies, product information and document repositories can be connected through suitable retrieval methods so responses are grounded in business-specific information.
Can it connect to our CRM, ERP or service system?
Yes, where appropriate APIs or integration mechanisms are available. The assistant can retrieve permitted context or initiate controlled actions based on the use case and security design.
What happens when the chatbot cannot resolve an enquiry?
The experience can clarify the request, offer alternate guidance or escalate to a person according to defined rules. Where supported, conversation context can be carried into the handoff.
Can the same assistant be used across more than one channel?
Potentially, yes. The core knowledge and service logic can support multiple compatible channels, while the interaction design may be adapted to each channelâs technical and user-experience constraints.
Can we start with only a few high-volume enquiries?
Yes. Starting with a focused set of well-understood intents is often a strong way to validate response quality, user adoption, escalation behavior and integration requirements before expanding scope.

chunks.page_title: AI Strategy & Consulting | Enterprise AI Roadmap | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Need clarity before making your next AI investment?
heading_path: Need clarity before making your next AI investment?
chunks.content:
Do we need to have an AI use case already identified?
No. The engagement can begin with business objectives, operational challenges and stakeholder interviews to discover and structure suitable opportunities before prioritization.
Can you review AI initiatives we have already started?
Yes. Existing pilots and ideas can be assessed against business value, technical feasibility, data readiness, integration requirements, governance and the path to production.
Will the strategy recommend specific AI platforms or models?
Where platform decisions are relevant, we can evaluate architectural options based on the use case, enterprise environment, security, integration and operating requirements rather than defaulting to one technology.
Can the engagement include data and knowledge readiness?
Yes. For prioritized use cases we can identify required data or knowledge sources, access constraints, quality concerns and gaps that must be addressed before implementation.
How do you approach AI governance?
Governance is aligned to what the AI is allowed to know, recommend or do. We consider permissions, human oversight, monitoring, traceability, escalation and the consequences of incorrect behavior.
Can Eureka also implement the roadmap afterward?
Yes. Where appropriate, the strategy can continue into proof-of-concept, application development, integration and production implementation, or it can remain an independent advisory engagement.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: Intelligent Document Processing | AI Document Automation | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning to automate a document-heavy business process?
heading_path: Planning to automate a document-heavy business process?
chunks.content:
How is Intelligent Document Processing different from basic OCR?
OCR primarily converts visible text into machine-readable text. IDP adds document classification, field or entity extraction, validation, exception handling and integration so the information can participate in a business process.
Can IDP handle documents with different layouts?
Often, yes. The appropriate method depends on document variability, content quality and required fields. AI-assisted extraction can handle more flexible layouts than fixed templates, but representative samples should be tested before defining expected performance.
What happens when the system is unsure about an extracted value?
Low-confidence or exception cases can be routed to a human review queue for verification or correction before data is released to downstream systems.
Can extracted data be validated against our ERP or master data?
Yes, where suitable integration access is available. Values can be checked against reference data, business rules or other system records before the document proceeds.
Can IDP process scanned PDFs and images?
Yes, subject to image quality, readability and the selected OCR/document technology. Representative samples should include the real scan conditions expected in production.
Can we begin with one document type such as invoices?
Yes. A well-defined document type with representative samples, clear target fields and known downstream processing is often an effective starting point before expanding to additional documents.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: Intelligent Workflow Automation | AI Workflow Solutions | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Considering AI for an existing workflow or automation process?
heading_path: Considering AI for an existing workflow or automation process?
chunks.content:
How is Intelligent Workflow Automation different from traditional workflow automation?
Traditional workflows work best with structured inputs and predefined rules. Intelligent workflow automation adds AI where the process needs to interpret language, documents or contextual information, while retaining deterministic workflow controls for predictable execution.
Does every workflow step need AI?
No. In most cases, only selected steps benefit from AI. Stable decisions, validations and system actions are often better implemented with conventional business rules and workflow logic.
Can AI route emails or requests to the right workflow?
Yes, where the input contains enough context. AI can classify suitable messages or requests by intent, category or priority and pass the result into controlled routing rules and queues.
Can people still review decisions before an action is taken?
Yes. Human review, approvals, corrections and overrides can be built into the workflow based on confidence, risk, business rules or exception conditions.
Can intelligent workflows connect to our existing applications?
Yes, where supported APIs, databases, workflow connectors or integration mechanisms are available. The architecture can coordinate actions across enterprise and custom systems.
Should we automate a complete process at once?
Not necessarily. A focused workflow or high-friction stage can be a practical starting point, especially where inputs, business rules and success criteria are well understood.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: Data Analytics & Visualization | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning to turn scattered business data into a more useful analytics experience?
heading_path: Planning to turn scattered business data into a more useful analytics experience?
chunks.content:
Can analytics combine data from multiple applications and databases?
Yes. Data from ERP, CRM, finance, operations, custom databases, files and other approved sources can be combined where suitable access and integration methods are available.
Do you only build analytics in Power BI?
No. Power BI is an important option, particularly in Microsoft environments, but we can also build custom web or embedded analytics when the experience needs to sit inside an application or portal.
Can users drill down and explore the data themselves?
Yes. Depending on the use case and data model, reports can include filters, drill-down, cross-filtering, comparisons and supporting detail while keeping the primary view clear.
Can you clean and transform inconsistent source data?
Yes. Data preparation can include mapping, cleaning, transformations and standardization. Where source-data quality issues cannot be safely corrected automatically, they are identified for business review rather than hidden inside the reporting layer.
Can analytics be embedded into an existing business application?
Yes. Where the selected platform and security model support it, analytics can be embedded within a portal or application so users can access insight closer to the workflow where decisions are made.
Can we add advanced or predictive analytics later?
Potentially, yes. Once the underlying data is sufficiently consistent and the business use case is clearly defined, appropriate statistical or predictive methods can be evaluated as a later stage rather than being added simply for complexity.

chunks.page_title: ESG & Sustainability Analytics | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning to move ESG reporting from spreadsheets to a structured analytics platform?
heading_path: Planning to move ESG reporting from spreadsheets to a structured analytics platform?
chunks.content:
Can the platform track Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 emissions?
Yes, where the organization has defined the required emission sources, boundaries, calculation approach and supporting activity data. Scope 3 coverage can be introduced according to the categories and source information that are realistically available.
Can ESG data be collected automatically from our existing systems?
Where suitable interfaces and reliable source data exist, yes. ERP, HR, production, databases and other approved systems can be integrated. Controlled manual capture can be retained for metrics that are not yet available digitally.
Can we track energy, water, waste and production intensity together?
Yes. Environmental measures can be analysed alongside production or other business activity where common sites, periods and dimensions can be mapped, enabling absolute and intensity-based views.
Can the solution also track CSR and community initiatives?
Yes. The data model can include initiatives such as community programmes, beneficiaries, contributions, training, equipment or other measurable social-impact activities relevant to the organization.
Can the analytics be aligned to our chosen ESG reporting framework?
Yes. Once your organization or ESG advisor has defined the applicable framework, metrics and reporting requirements, we can map the data model and outputs to those requirements. Eurekaâs role is the technology, data and analytics implementation rather than independent ESG certification or assurance.
Can the platform track sustainability improvement projects and targets?
Yes. Baselines, targets, initiatives, owners, expected impact and progress can be brought into management views so sustainability reporting connects more directly with improvement activity.

chunks.section_heading: Planning to consolidate management reporting into executive dashboards?
heading_path: Planning to consolidate management reporting into executive dashboards?
chunks.content:
Can an executive dashboard combine data from multiple systems?
Yes. Data from ERP, CRM, finance, operations, custom databases and other approved sources can be integrated where suitable access and interfaces are available.
Do you only build dashboards in Power BI?
No. Power BI is one strong option, particularly in Microsoft environments. We can also build custom web-based dashboard experiences when the use case requires deeper application integration or a tailored management portal.
Can different executives see different dashboard views?
Yes. Dashboards can be organized by role, function, entity or responsibility, with appropriate access controls and shared enterprise KPIs where required.
Can users drill down from an executive KPI into more detail?
Yes, where the data model supports it. We can design drill-down paths, filters and supporting views so users can investigate the drivers behind a headline measure without cluttering the executive overview.
How often can dashboard data refresh?
Refresh frequency depends on source-system capability, integration method, data volume, platform limits and the actual management need. We define an appropriate refresh approach during data mapping rather than assuming every KPI needs real-time data.
Can you help define KPIs if our management reporting is still evolving?
Yes. We can work with stakeholders to clarify reporting questions, metric definitions, targets, calculation logic and source ownership before dashboard development begins.

Can financial analytics combine data from our ERP and other systems?

Can we analyse budget vs actual performance?
Yes. We can model budgets and actuals using agreed account, entity, department, product or other business dimensions and provide absolute, percentage and period-based variance analysis.
Can reports show profitability by customer, product or business unit?
Yes, provided the underlying revenue and cost data can be mapped at the required level. We first validate allocation logic and data availability so profitability views remain meaningful and reconcilable.
Can you build cash-flow and working-capital reporting?
Yes. Depending on available data, reporting can cover cash position and movement, receivables, payables, ageing, collections and other working-capital indicators relevant to management.
Do we need Power BI for financial analytics?
No. Power BI is a strong option for interactive finance analysis, but we can also create custom web reporting or structured Excel and PDF outputs where the workflow requires them.
How do you ensure the dashboard numbers match finance reports?
We define calculation logic and source mapping with stakeholders, then reconcile agreed measures against trusted source reports and investigate material differences before adoption.

chunks.page_title: KPI & MIS Reporting | Management Reporting Solutions | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning to standardize or automate recurring KPI and MIS reporting?
heading_path: Planning to standardize or automate recurring KPI and MIS reporting?
chunks.content:
Can you automate an MIS process that currently runs in Excel?
Often, yes. We first review the existing workbook logic, data sources, manual steps, exceptions and reporting controls. Suitable parts can then be moved into a governed reporting model while retaining Excel outputs where they remain useful.
Can one MIS report combine data from multiple systems?
Yes. Data can be brought together from ERP, CRM, finance, operations, databases, files and other approved sources where suitable interfaces and access are available.
Can reports run daily, weekly and monthly?
Yes, where the source data and reporting need support those frequencies. We recommend a cadence based on management requirements and source availability rather than assuming every KPI requires the same refresh cycle.
Can we continue receiving Excel or PDF reports?
Yes. Interactive dashboards do not have to replace every familiar format. We can retain structured Excel or PDF outputs where they support established review, distribution or control processes.
What if different departments define the same KPI differently?
We surface those differences during KPI definition and work with stakeholders to agree the business rule, calculation, dimensions, source and ownership. The agreed definition can then be documented in a KPI dictionary.
Can Power BI dashboards and traditional MIS packs coexist?
Yes. Power BI can provide interactive analysis while structured MIS packs support recurring management meetings, distribution and archival needs. Both can be built on the same governed reporting logic where appropriate.

chunks.page_title: Power BI Solutions | Consulting, Dashboards & Analytics | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning a new Power BI solution or improving an existing one?
heading_path: Planning a new Power BI solution or improving an existing one?
chunks.content:
Can Power BI connect to our existing ERP, CRM and SQL databases?
Power BI supports many data-source and connection patterns. We assess your source systems, access methods, security and reporting requirements to determine an appropriate integration approach.
Can you migrate our Excel-based management reports to Power BI?
Yes. We first review the existing calculations, source data and report purpose, then redesign the model and visuals for Power BI rather than simply reproducing spreadsheet layouts screen for screen.
Can different users see different data in the same Power BI report?
Yes. Power BI supports role-based security patterns including row-level security. The exact design depends on the semantic model, user roles and deployment architecture.
Can Power BI reports be embedded inside our web application or portal?
Yes. Microsoft provides Power BI embedded analytics options for integrating reports and analytics into applications. The appropriate embedding and authentication model depends on whether users are internal or external and on the deployment requirements.
Can you improve slow or difficult-to-maintain Power BI reports?
Yes. We can review data models, relationships, DAX, transformations, visual design and refresh patterns to identify practical areas for simplification or performance improvement.
Do we need to decide Power BI licensing before starting?
Licensing and capacity should be confirmed against your user groups, sharing model, embedding needs and Microsoftâs current licensing terms. We can help identify the technical usage pattern, while final licensing should be validated against the applicable Microsoft offering.

chunks.page_title: Application Support & Maintenance | Eureka Solutions
heading_path: Planning Ongoing Application Support?
chunks.content:
Is this a helpdesk or end-user support service?
This page is focused on engineering-led application support and maintenance rather than a generic end-user helpdesk. The exact responsibility boundary is agreed for each engagement and can include application defects, technical investigation, maintenance, releases and planned enhancements.
Can Eureka take over an application developed by another vendor?
Yes, subject to a structured assessment and transition. We first understand the codebase, architecture, integrations, environments, documentation, current issues and available knowledge before agreeing the support operating model.
Can support include enhancements and new features?
Yes. Many long-term application engagements combine production support with planned improvements. We keep urgent operational work visible alongside enhancements so both stability and business change can be managed deliberately.
Do you support older or legacy applications?
Yes. Eureka works across established Microsoft/.NET, Java and PHP/LAMP environments as well as modern application stacks. We assess the actual technology, maintainability and operational risks before defining the right support approach.
How do you handle response times and support hours?
Coverage windows, priority definitions, response expectations and escalation paths are agreed around the applicationâs business criticality and engagement model. They should be explicit rather than implied.
Can your team work with our internal IT or engineering team?
Yes. We can operate as an extension of internal technology teams, collaborating on priorities, environments, releases, security requirements and areas where ownership remains with the client or another specialist provider.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: Dedicated Development Teams | Eureka Solutions
heading_path: Considering a dedicated development team?
chunks.content:
How is a dedicated development team different from staff augmentation?
Staff augmentation usually adds individual specialists into a client-managed team. A dedicated development team can include a balanced group of engineers working together around a product or workstream, with an agreed delivery cadence and shared accountability. Eureka can support either shape depending on what your organisation needs.
Will we manage the dedicated team directly?
The working model is agreed with you. Product priorities and business decisions remain close to your organisation, while day-to-day engineering planning, technical coordination and delivery responsibilities can be shared between your leads and Eureka depending on the engagement shape.
Can we start with a smaller team and scale later?
Yes. The team can begin around the immediate engineering need and evolve as the roadmap becomes clearer. We prefer changes in team shape to follow real workload and capability requirements rather than committing to unnecessary roles from the start.
Can the team work with our existing tools and development process?
Yes. Where practical, the team can work within your existing planning, source-control, communication and delivery practices. If the current process needs more structure, we can agree a practical shared cadence rather than imposing ceremony for its own sake.
Can dedicated teams support an existing product, not just build something new?
Yes. A dedicated team can take on enhancement, modernisation, integration, technical debt, support-oriented engineering or a defined product workstream. We first invest in understanding the existing architecture and operating context before expecting the team to work independently.
Can Eureka provide onsite participation?
Where the programme benefits from it and the engagement allows, focused onsite participation can be planned around high-value stages such as discovery, requirements, UAT or go-live while the ongoing engineering team continues through the agreed delivery model.

chunks.page_title: Engineering Team Augmentation | Eureka Solutions
heading_path: Considering engineering team augmentation?
chunks.content:
Who manages an augmented engineer day to day?
In a typical augmentation model, the engineer works inside the clientâs existing team and delivery structure. Your product and technical leads retain direction over priorities and architecture, while Eureka supports the engagement and staffing relationship.
How is this different from a dedicated development team?
Augmentation adds targeted engineers into a team you already operate. A dedicated development team is a broader, more self-contained engineering unit assembled around a product or workstream. The right choice depends mainly on how much delivery structure already exists on your side.
Can we augment our team with Java or PHP/LAMP engineers as well as .NET resources?
Yes. Eurekaâs augmentation coverage includes Microsoft/.NET, Java and PHP/LAMP capabilities, along with frontend, mobile, quality, data, BI, AI, APIs and integration skills depending on the requirement.
Can augmented engineers work with our existing tools and processes?
Yes. That is the preferred model. Where access and client policies allow, engineers work within the existing planning, communication, source-control, review and delivery practices used by your team.
Can we add more engineers later?
Yes. Capacity can be reviewed as roadmap needs change. We recommend adding roles because the work requires them rather than building a larger augmentation footprint than the client team can meaningfully absorb.
Can augmented engineers work across time zones?
Working overlap is agreed around the client location, collaboration needs and role. Eureka has delivery experience with clients across India, Africa, the UK, US, Europe, Singapore and Australia, and we shape the communication model accordingly.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: Managed Technology Services | Eureka Solutions
heading_path: Considering a Managed Technology Service?
chunks.content:
How is this different from a dedicated development team?
With a dedicated team, the client typically manages day-to-day work and uses Eureka engineers as part of its delivery organization. In a managed technology service, Eureka takes responsibility for coordinating an agreed service boundary, including delivery visibility, engineering work, governance and improvement according to the engagement model.
Do we have to outsource our entire technology function?
No. The scope can be one application, a platform capability, an integration landscape or a defined portfolio. The most important requirement is that responsibility boundaries between Eureka, the client and any other providers are explicit.
Can managed services include both support and new development?
Yes. A managed service can combine operational support, maintenance, defect resolution, enhancements and planned engineering improvement. The balance is defined around the technology estate and business roadmap.
Do you provide 24Ã7 support and fixed SLAs?
Coverage windows, priority definitions, response expectations, escalation paths and any service-level commitments are agreed for the specific engagement. We do not assume one standard coverage model fits every application or client.
Can Eureka work alongside our internal IT team and other vendors?
Yes. Managed technology often operates in a multi-team environment. We define interfaces, ownership and escalation points so Eureka can manage its service responsibilities while collaborating with internal teams and specialist providers.
How do you take over an existing technology service?
We begin with discovery and transition: mapping applications and dependencies, establishing access, reviewing documentation and current issues, transferring knowledge, agreeing governance and creating the initial operational and improvement backlog before moving into steady-state service.

chunks.page_title: Offshore Development Center (ODC) | Eureka Solutions
heading_path: Considering an Offshore Development Center?
chunks.content:
How is an ODC different from a dedicated development team?
A dedicated development team is usually a focused engineering unit around one product or workstream. An ODC is a broader offshore capability that can include multiple squads, centre-level leadership, shared engineering practices and governance across a portfolio. A dedicated team can also evolve into an ODC as the offshore footprint grows.
Do we need to start with a large ODC?
Not necessarily. The initial structure should match the actual portfolio and workload. The centre can begin with a focused core and expand as the roadmap, product ownership and offshore operating model mature.
Who manages the ODC?
The operating model is agreed with the client. Product priorities and major technology decisions remain closely connected to client leadership, while Eureka can coordinate offshore delivery leadership, staffing, engineering practices and centre operations according to the engagement scope.
Can the ODC support different technologies and product teams?
Yes. Eurekaâs engineering breadth includes Microsoft/.NET, Java, PHP/LAMP, frontend, mobile, QA, data, BI, AI, APIs and integration capabilities, allowing different squads to be shaped around their product environments.
How do you handle security and access in an ODC model?
Security and access are designed around the client environment and engagement requirements. This can include client-approved identity and access controls, repository and environment permissions, information-handling practices and appropriate contractual confidentiality and IP provisions.
Can ODC teams work with our onsite teams or participate onsite?
Yes. The collaboration model can include defined working-hour overlap and focused onsite participation where it adds value, such as discovery, requirements, UAT, go-live or other critical programme stages.

chunks.page_title: Project Rescue & Takeover | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Considering a Project Rescue or Takeover?
heading_path: Considering a Project Rescue or Takeover?
chunks.content:
How do you know whether the existing application can be rescued?
We assess the actual codebase, architecture, data, integrations, environments, functional completeness, defects and delivery context. The recommendation may be to continue largely as-is, remediate selected areas, re-scope delivery or selectively rebuild where the evidence justifies it.
Can Eureka take over from our current software vendor?
Yes. We structure the transition around access, project assets, environments, documentation, backlog and knowledge capture. Where possible, we work professionally with the outgoing team to preserve continuity and reduce unnecessary disruption.
Do we need complete documentation before you can start?
No. Incomplete documentation is common in rescue situations. Available material is useful, but we can also reconstruct understanding through code, environments, data, issue history, product walkthroughs and discussions with people who know the system.
Will you recommend rebuilding the project?
Only when the evidence supports it. A rewrite carries its own cost and risk. We prefer to identify what is genuinely usable, what needs remediation and what cannot responsibly support the required outcome before recommending major replacement work.
Can you rescue a live production application as well as an unfinished project?
Yes. The recovery priorities differ. A live application may require immediate operational stabilisation and controlled change, while an unfinished project may focus first on functional completeness, release readiness and a credible delivery baseline.
What happens after the rescue is complete?
The recovered project can transition to the client team, continue with a dedicated Eureka delivery team, or move into an application support and maintenance model. The right end-state is agreed around the clientâs longer-term ownership plan.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: Business Process Automation Solutions | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning a business process automation initiative?
heading_path: Planning a business process automation initiative?
chunks.content:
What business processes can be automated?
Processes with repeatable steps, defined rules, approvals, data movement or regular follow-ups are strong candidates. Common examples include purchase requests, invoice processing, employee onboarding, document approvals, service requests, notifications and management reporting.
When should we use Power Automate instead of custom development?
Power Automate is effective for many Microsoft 365 and structured workflow scenarios where rapid delivery is important. Custom development is better when a process needs complex logic, high transaction volumes, specialized interfaces or deeper control. We can also combine both approaches.
Can automation integrate with our existing or legacy systems?
Yes. We use APIs, database integration, scheduled services, file exchange, connectors and other integration methods to automate processes across modern and legacy applications.
Can email and Excel-based workflows be automated?
Yes. Many automation initiatives begin by replacing email approvals and spreadsheet trackers with structured forms, workflows, notifications, centralized data and real-time status visibility.
How long does a business process automation project take?
The timeline depends on process complexity, number of integrations, exception paths and user groups. A focused workflow can often be delivered much faster than a large cross-functional automation program, so we usually recommend prioritizing high-value processes and rolling out in phases.
Can AI be added to existing workflows?
Yes. AI can be introduced for document extraction, classification, summarization, decision support, intelligent routing and agent-assisted tasks while keeping approvals, governance and business rules under defined control.

chunks.page_title: Enterprise Document Management Solutions | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning an enterprise document management initiative?
heading_path: Planning an enterprise document management initiative?
chunks.content:
How is an EDMS different from a shared drive?
A shared drive mainly stores files. An EDMS adds structured metadata, version control, permissions, search, workflows, audit history, retention controls and governance so documents can be managed through their complete lifecycle.
Should we use SharePoint or build a custom EDMS?
SharePoint is a strong fit for many Microsoft 365 environments and common document-management scenarios. A custom EDMS may be better where specialized workflows, interfaces, scale, security models or integration requirements go beyond the standard platform. We evaluate both approaches around the business need.
Can existing documents be migrated from shared drives or legacy systems?
Yes. We assess the source repositories, identify duplicates and obsolete content, define metadata and mapping rules, then migrate documents in controlled stages with validation before cutover.
Can access be controlled by department, role or document type?
Yes. Permissions can be designed around organizational roles, departments, document categories, confidentiality levels and business rules while maintaining appropriate administrative and audit controls.
Can retention, archival and audit requirements be managed?
Yes. EDMS solutions can apply retention policies, archival rules, version history, activity logs and other governance controls according to your organizational and regulatory requirements.
Can document workflows integrate with ERP and other applications?
Yes. Documents and approvals can be connected with ERP, CRM, Microsoft 365 and other applications through APIs, connectors, databases and workflow services so information remains part of the wider business process.

chunks.page_title: Enterprise ERP Solutions & Custom ERP Development | Eureka Solutions
heading_path: Planning an ERP initiative?
chunks.content:
How long does a custom ERP implementation take?
The timeline depends on scope, integrations, data migration and rollout strategy. We normally recommend phased delivery so priority capabilities can go live earlier while the wider platform continues to evolve.
Can the ERP integrate with our existing systems?
Yes. We design APIs and integrations for finance platforms, CRM systems, Microsoft 365, payment services, banking interfaces, mobile apps and other enterprise applications.
Can ERP modules be deployed in phases?
Yes. A modular approach lets you begin with high-priority functions such as finance, procurement or inventory, then add additional capabilities as users and processes mature.
Do you support cloud and on-premise deployment?
Yes. The solution can be deployed in the cloud, on-premise or through a hybrid model based on your security, compliance and infrastructure requirements.
How is legacy data migrated?
We assess source data, define cleansing and mapping rules, perform controlled trial migrations and validate balances and records with business users before production cutover.
Do you provide post-go-live support?
Yes. We provide hypercare, application support, enhancements, reporting improvements, integrations and ongoing platform modernization after implementation.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: HR & Payroll Solutions | Custom HRMS | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning an HR or payroll modernization initiative?
heading_path: Planning an HR or payroll modernization initiative?
chunks.content:
Can the HRMS be customized around our HR policies?
Yes. Leave rules, approval paths, employee categories, organization structures, workflows, forms and other HR processes can be configured around your operating model rather than forcing every organization into the same process.
Can payroll rules be configured for different organizations or locations?
Yes. Salary structures, allowances, deductions and payroll rules can be configured for defined employee groups and entities. Country-specific statutory requirements should be assessed and configured for the jurisdictions in which the solution will operate.
Can the system integrate with biometric or attendance devices?
Yes. Where the device or attendance platform provides a usable API, database, file interface or integration mechanism, attendance data can be connected with HR workflows and payroll inputs.
Can employees use self-service for leave, claims and payslips?
Yes. Employee self-service can provide secure access to personal information, leave requests, claims, payslips, letters and other HR services based on the modules implemented.
Can existing employee and payroll data be migrated?
Yes. We assess source data, define mapping and cleansing rules, migrate employee masters and agreed historical information, and validate the results before production cutover.
Can HR and payroll integrate with finance or ERP systems?
Yes. Approved payroll outputs, cost allocations, employee information and other required data can be exchanged with ERP, finance, identity and reporting systems through APIs, files, databases or other supported integration methods.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: Inventory & Warehouse Management Solutions | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning an inventory or warehouse modernization initiative?
heading_path: Planning an inventory or warehouse modernization initiative?
chunks.content:
Can the system manage multiple warehouses and locations?
Yes. Inventory can be structured across multiple warehouses, stores, zones, bins or other operational locations with stock balances and movements tracked at the required level.
Can we track batches, serial numbers and expiry dates?
Yes. Where required by the inventory model, items can carry batch, lot, serial or expiry information so receipts, issues, transfers and stock history remain traceable.
Can barcode or QR scanning be used in warehouse transactions?
Yes. Scanning can be incorporated into receiving, put-away, picking, transfers, stock counts and other workflows when the item and location labelling approach supports it.
Can the inventory system integrate with our ERP or procurement system?
Yes. Inventory movements, purchase receipts, orders, production consumption and financial information can be exchanged with ERP and other systems through APIs, databases, files or supported integration services.
Can existing item masters and opening stock be migrated?
Yes. We define mapping and cleansing rules for item masters, locations and opening balances, then validate migrated quantities and values with business users before production cutover.
Can we define reorder levels and stock alerts?
Yes. Reorder thresholds, stock ageing, low-stock conditions and other operational alerts can be configured around the inventory rules and data available in the implemented solution.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: Dynamics 365 Solutions | CRM, Business Apps & Integration | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning a Dynamics 365 implementation, extension or integration?
heading_path: Planning a Dynamics 365 implementation, extension or integration?
chunks.content:
Which Dynamics 365 application should we start with?
Start with the business process and users, not the product catalogue. Dynamics 365 includes multiple applications covering sales, service, field operations, finance and other functions. We map the requirement to the relevant capabilities before recommending the implementation scope.
Can Dynamics 365 integrate with our existing ERP or other applications?
Yes, in many scenarios. The appropriate pattern depends on the Dynamics application, the external system, data ownership, timing, volumes and available APIs or integration capabilities. We define the system-of-record boundaries before designing interfaces.
Can Power Apps and Power Automate extend Dynamics 365?
Yes. Dynamics 365 customer-engagement apps and Power Platform share important foundations, including Dataverse. Power Apps and Power Automate can support adjacent applications and workflows where they provide a cleaner extension path than deeper core customization.
Can you migrate data from our current CRM?
Yes. We assess source quality, duplicates, mappings, ownership, history and business value before defining what should migrate. Data migration should include cleansing, reconciliation and business validation rather than a raw table-to-table transfer.
Can you take over an existing Dynamics 365 environment?
Yes. We can review the current configuration, solutions, Dataverse structure, security, flows, integrations, reports and pain points, then recommend whether to stabilize, simplify or extend the environment.
How do we avoid over-customizing Dynamics 365?
Use a fit-to-standard mindset first. Prefer supported native capabilities and configuration, use Power Platform for appropriate adjacent needs, and reserve deeper customization for requirements that create enough business value to justify the lifecycle cost.

chunks.page_title: Power BI Solutions | Dashboards, Reporting & Analytics | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning a new Power BI solution or improving an existing one?
heading_path: Planning a new Power BI solution or improving an existing one?
chunks.content:
Can Power BI connect to our ERP, CRM, SQL databases and other business systems?
Power BI supports many data-source and connection patterns. We assess source systems, access methods, security, refresh expectations and reporting needs to determine an appropriate integration approach.
Can you migrate our Excel-based management reports to Power BI?
Yes. We review the existing calculations, source data and reporting purpose first, then redesign the model and report experience for Power BI rather than reproducing spreadsheet layouts screen for screen.
Can different users see different data in the same report?
Yes. Power BI supports model security patterns including row-level security. The correct design depends on the semantic model, user roles, workspace permissions and deployment architecture.
Can Power BI reports be embedded in our web application or portal?
Yes. Microsoft provides embedded analytics options for integrating Power BI into applications. The appropriate authentication, licensing and embedding model depends on the audience and application scenario.
Can you improve slow or difficult-to-maintain Power BI reports?
Yes. We can review source queries, transformations, semantic models, relationships, DAX measures, refresh patterns and report design to identify practical areas for simplification and performance improvement.
Do we need Microsoft Fabric for every Power BI project?
No. Power BI can be implemented without making every engagement a Fabric programme. Where Microsoft Fabric is already part of the data architecture or creates clear value, we can design Power BI to fit that wider environment.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: Power Apps Development | Microsoft Power Platform Solutions | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Considering Power Apps for an internal business application?
heading_path: Considering Power Apps for an internal business application?
chunks.content:
Should we build a canvas app or a model-driven app?
It depends on the experience and data model. Canvas apps provide greater control over the screen and task experience, while model-driven apps are well suited to structured, data-centric solutions built on Dataverse. We decide after reviewing the process, users, data and security requirements.
Does every Power App need Dataverse?
No. Canvas apps can work with a range of supported data sources. Dataverse is especially useful when the solution needs structured business data, relationships, security and broader Power Platform capabilities. The data source should be chosen for the requirement rather than by default.
Can Power Apps connect to our existing systems?
Often, yes. Power Platform provides connectors for many services, and custom connectors can expose appropriate APIs where a prebuilt connector is not available. Integration feasibility depends on the target system, authentication, network access and API capabilities.
Can Power Apps replace Excel or Microsoft Access applications?
For many departmental tracking and process applications, Power Apps can provide a more structured, shared and governed experience. We first assess the data volume, business logic, integrations, offline needs and reporting expectations before recommending a replacement.
Can Power Apps trigger approvals and notifications?
Yes. Power Automate is commonly used alongside Power Apps for approvals, notifications, background workflows and integrations. We separate app interaction from workflow orchestration so each tool is used where it fits best.
Can you take over an existing Power App that has become difficult to maintain?
Yes. We can review the current app, formulas, flows, connections, data sources, security and environment setup, then recommend whether to stabilize, refactor or rebuild the solution.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: Power Automate Solutions | Workflow Automation & RPA | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning Power Automate for a business-critical workflow?
heading_path: Planning Power Automate for a business-critical workflow?
chunks.content:
What is the difference between a cloud flow and a desktop flow?
Cloud flows automate processes across supported services using triggers, schedules, actions, connectors and APIs. Desktop flows automate suitable tasks through a Windows desktop interface and are useful when a legacy application does not provide an appropriate API. We prefer the more supportable integration pattern for each scenario.
Can Power Automate handle multi-stage approvals?
Yes. Approval workflows can include human decision points, routing and downstream actions. The exact design depends on approval rules, sequencing, delegation, escalation, audit requirements and how the process should behave when a request is rejected or changed.
Can Power Automate connect to our existing applications?
Often, yes. Power Automate provides a broad connector ecosystem and can use appropriate custom connectors or APIs for systems that expose suitable interfaces. On-premises connectivity and network constraints should be reviewed during solution design.
Should we use desktop automation whenever an old system has no integration?
Not automatically. Desktop automation can be valuable for suitable non-API tasks, but it introduces dependencies on the application interface and execution environment. We assess stability, volumes, exception handling and support needs before recommending RPA.
Can you take over existing flows that are failing or difficult to maintain?
Yes. We can review flow design, connections, ownership, run history, error handling, environment setup and dependent systems, then recommend whether to stabilize, refactor or rebuild the automation.
How is Power Automate licensed?
Licensing depends on the capabilities used, including connector types, users, process requirements and desktop automation scenarios. We identify the relevant technical pattern first and confirm current Microsoft licensing implications before implementation.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: Power Pages Development | Customer & Partner Portals | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Considering Power Pages for an external business portal?
heading_path: Considering Power Pages for an external business portal?
chunks.content:
Is Power Pages only for authenticated portals?
No. Power Pages can support public/anonymous experiences as well as authenticated users. The right model depends on what content and data should be visible and whether users need personalized or protected access.
Does Power Pages use Dataverse?
Yes. Dataverse is the core business-data platform behind Power Pages. Forms, lists and other portal experiences can work with Dataverse data, subject to the security and permission model configured for the site.
Can different customers or partners see only their own records?
Yes, when the Dataverse relationships, web roles and table permissions are designed correctly. We define the access model explicitly and test it with realistic user roles before launch.
Can Power Pages trigger approvals or internal workflows?
Yes. Power Automate can be used alongside Power Pages and Dataverse so portal submissions or data changes can initiate notifications, reviews, approvals and downstream processing where appropriate.
Should we use Power Pages instead of a custom web application?
Not automatically. Power Pages is compelling when the external experience is closely tied to Dataverse and Power Platform processes. Highly specialized consumer experiences, unusual architecture, very custom interaction models or other technical constraints may justify a custom web application instead.
How is Power Pages licensed?
Licensing depends on the usage model and current Microsoft terms, including how authenticated and anonymous access is consumed. We define the portal scenario first and confirm the applicable Microsoft licensing and capacity approach before production rollout.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: SharePoint Solutions | Microsoft 365 Consulting & Development | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning a new SharePoint solution or modernizing an existing environment?
heading_path: Planning a new SharePoint solution or modernizing an existing environment?
chunks.content:
Do you work with both SharePoint Online and older on-premises SharePoint environments?
Yes. We have experience with SharePoint on-premises as well as Microsoft 365. For modernization projects, we assess the current sites, content, permissions, customizations and workflows before defining an appropriate target architecture.
Can you migrate SharePoint Server content to Microsoft 365?
Yes. Microsoft provides SharePoint migration tooling for supported on-premises scenarios. We combine the migration mechanics with assessment, target design, content decisions, permission mapping, validation and business testing.
Can SharePoint replace our document management system?
For some organizations and use cases, SharePoint provides a strong document-management foundation through libraries, metadata, versioning, permissions and Microsoft 365 integration. More specialized regulatory, records or workflow requirements should be assessed before deciding whether native SharePoint is the right fit.
Can SharePoint approvals be automated?
Yes. Power Automate supports approval and workflow scenarios around SharePoint lists, libraries and content. We decide whether the process belongs in Power Automate based on its complexity, duration, integrations and governance requirements.
Can you build custom functionality in modern SharePoint?
Yes. Where configuration and Power Platform do not adequately meet the requirement, modern SharePoint can be extended using supported development patterns such as SharePoint Framework.
Should every department get its own SharePoint site?
Not automatically. Site structure should reflect ownership, collaboration boundaries, information architecture, navigation and governance. We define the site and hub model before creating sites at scale.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: API Development & Integration | System Integration | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning a new API or untangling an existing integration?
heading_path: Planning a new API or untangling an existing integration?
chunks.content:
Can you integrate systems from different vendors and technology stacks?
Yes, where the systems provide suitable interfaces or other supported integration mechanisms. We first assess the APIs, data formats, authentication options, transaction volumes and operational constraints on both sides before selecting an approach.
Do you only build REST APIs?
No. REST is common, but the right approach depends on the systems and the transaction. An integration may use synchronous APIs, webhooks, asynchronous events, scheduled exchange or other supported mechanisms. We avoid choosing a pattern simply because it is fashionable.
Can you work with an API that already exists?
Yes. We can review an existing interface and its consumers, document current behaviour, identify reliability or security concerns, and plan improvements without unnecessarily breaking dependent applications.
How do you handle failures between systems?
The strategy depends on the transaction. It may include controlled timeouts, retries, idempotent operations, asynchronous processing, dead-letter handling, reconciliation and alerting. The important point is to define failure behaviour deliberately rather than leaving it to chance.
Can APIs be used by our mobile apps, portals or partners?
Yes, when designed for those consumers with the right access controls, contract boundaries and exposure model. Public or partner-facing interfaces generally need different security and lifecycle considerations from purely internal APIs.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: Enterprise System Integration | Connected Applications & Data | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning to connect a fragmented enterprise landscape?
heading_path: Planning to connect a fragmented enterprise landscape?
chunks.content:
Do we need to replace our legacy systems before integrating them?
Not necessarily. If a legacy application remains important and offers a supportable way to exchange data or transactions, an integration boundary can help modern applications work around it while a longer-term modernization plan proceeds separately.
Should every application connect directly to every other application?
Usually not. Point-to-point connections can be appropriate for simple cases, but uncontrolled growth creates tight coupling and difficult change impact. We assess where a defined integration layer, reusable service or asynchronous pattern provides a cleaner boundary.
How do you decide which system owns a piece of data?
We look at the business process, who creates and maintains the record, where authoritative decisions occur and which system is accountable for its lifecycle. That ownership is agreed before deciding how copies or views should be synchronized elsewhere.
Can enterprise integration include cloud and on-premise systems together?
Yes, subject to the security, networking and interface capabilities of the systems involved. Hybrid landscapes are common, so the design must account for connectivity, authentication, latency, availability and operational ownership across both environments.
How should we start if we already have many undocumented integrations?
Start with a landscape and dependency map. We identify business-critical flows, existing interfaces, manual workarounds, recurring failures and system owners, then prioritize improvements by operational risk and business value rather than attempting to replace everything simultaneously.

chunks.page_title: Legacy Application Modernization | Modernize Business Systems | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Thinking about replacing or modernizing a long-running application?
heading_path: Thinking about replacing or modernizing a long-running application?
chunks.content:
How do we know whether to refactor or completely rebuild our application?
We compare the current applicationâs business value with its technical constraints. If the architecture remains workable and the problems are localized, refactoring may be enough. If maintainability, security, scalability or change cost is constrained across the core system, a bounded or full rebuild may create better long-term value.
Do we need to migrate all historical data into the new system?
Not always. We classify data by operational need, reporting or audit value, legal retention requirements and migration cost. Some history may need full migration, some may remain in a controlled archive and some may no longer justify carrying forward.
Can the old and new applications run together during modernization?
Yes, in many cases. A staged transition can use APIs, controlled synchronization or clear functional boundaries so selected modules move first. The design must prevent unclear ownership or uncontrolled data duplication while both environments coexist.
Can you modernize an application even if documentation is poor?
Yes, although discovery becomes especially important. We combine available documentation with code, database, interface and user-process analysis to reconstruct how the application behaves. Critical business rules should be validated with knowledgeable users before being reimplemented.
Should modernization automatically mean moving to the cloud?
No. Hosting is one architectural decision, not the definition of modernization. The right target depends on security, operations, integration, availability, cost and organizational constraints. An application can be meaningfully modernized without forcing a cloud move that the business does not need.

chunks.page_title: Microsoft 365 Integration | Graph, SharePoint, Teams & Business Systems | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning to connect an enterprise application with Microsoft 365?
heading_path: Planning to connect an enterprise application with Microsoft 365?
chunks.content:
What is Microsoft Graph and why is it relevant to Microsoft 365 integration?
Microsoft Graph is Microsoftâs gateway to data and services across Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Entra, among other Microsoft cloud services. It provides REST APIs and SDKs for supported scenarios involving resources such as files, mail, calendar, SharePoint and Teams.
Can our application access Microsoft 365 without a user being signed in?
Some Microsoft Graph scenarios support application-only access, while others use delegated access on behalf of a signed-in user. The correct model depends on the API, resource and business scenario, and the application must be granted the required permissions through Microsoftâs authorization model.
Can we connect our ERP or custom application with SharePoint documents?
Yes, where the required SharePoint and Microsoft Graph capabilities support the scenario. We first define which system owns the business record, where the document belongs, how users should access it and which permissions the integration genuinely requires.
Can Microsoft Teams receive information from our business applications?
There are supported ways to bring appropriate business context and application experiences into Microsoft Teams, depending on the scenario. We choose the pattern based on what users need to see or do rather than treating Teams as a replacement for the underlying transaction system.
Do we need very broad Microsoft 365 permissions for integration?
Not by default. Microsoft recommends requesting the least privileged permissions required for the application to function. We start from the specific operation and resource, then design the consent and access model around the narrowest suitable permissions.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: Third-Party Integrations | APIs, SaaS & External Platforms | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Need to connect a business system with an external platform?
heading_path: Need to connect a business system with an external platform?
chunks.content:
Can you integrate with any third-party platform?
It depends on what the provider makes available. We first review its supported APIs or integration mechanisms, authentication model, documentation, limits and commercial access conditions. If the platform does not provide a suitable supported interface, we will identify that constraint before proposing a solution.
What if the provider changes its API later?
We try to contain provider-specific contracts behind a clear boundary so changes affect fewer parts of your application. Versioning and change notices still need to be monitored, tested and released deliberately; no architecture can eliminate a provider dependency entirely.
How do you handle a third-party service outage?
The right response depends on the business transaction. Options may include controlled retries, queued processing, fallback behaviour, user-visible pending states, reconciliation or alerts. We define this behaviour during integration design rather than leaving it to generic exception handling.
Can you replace one third-party provider with another later?
Potentially. Keeping provider-specific logic separated can make replacement easier, but providers rarely expose identical capabilities or contracts. A future switch will still require mapping, testing and business validation for the new service.
Can you take over an existing third-party integration that is unreliable?
Yes. We can review the current connector, logs, failure patterns, provider documentation, authentication, error handling and reconciliation process, then recommend whether the integration should be stabilized, redesigned or replaced.

chunks.page_title: Customer & Partner Portal Development | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning a customer or partner portal?
heading_path: Planning a customer or partner portal?
chunks.content:
What is the difference between a customer portal and a partner portal?
A customer portal is typically designed around service, account, transaction and relationship journeys for customers. A partner portal supports organisations such as vendors, distributors, dealers or other business partners, often with different workflows, data access and collaboration needs. Both can share a common technical foundation while presenting distinct experiences.
Can the portal show live information from our ERP or CRM?
Yes, when the source system provides appropriate integration interfaces. We define the system of record, API contract, permissions, performance expectations and failure behaviour so the portal can surface current business information without becoming an uncontrolled duplicate of the backend system.
Can different customers or partners see different data and functionality?
Yes. Role, organisation, account and relationship context can be used to control permitted data and actions. The exact model is designed around your identity source, business rules and security requirements.
Can users upload and access documents through the portal?
Yes. Document upload, download, review and association can be designed into portal workflows, with storage location, permissions, metadata and document ownership defined according to the underlying platform and business need.
Can we start with a few portal services and expand later?
Yes. A phased rollout is often practical. We can establish the portal foundation around high-value journeys first and extend additional workflows, integrations and user groups as adoption grows.

Can the commerce platform integrate with our ERP or inventory system?
Yes, where suitable APIs or integration interfaces are available or can be created. We define clear ownership for products, customers, stock, pricing and orders so the commerce layer uses reliable enterprise data without unnecessarily duplicating the source system.
Can you integrate online payments?
Yes, appropriate payment services can be integrated according to the selected providerâs supported interfaces and your business requirements. We design the transaction around authorized success, failure, cancellation and recovery paths rather than treating payment as a simple button.
Can the platform support account-specific B2B pricing?
Yes, if the business pricing rules and source data support it. We can design account-aware pricing and purchasing experiences with the relevant data and authorization boundaries.
Can eCommerce analytics be connected to our business reporting?
Yes. Commerce activity and transaction data can be brought into appropriate reporting and analytics models so teams can compare journey behaviour with orders, revenue, product and operational outcomes.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: Enterprise Web Application Development | Eureka Solutions
heading_path: Planning an enterprise web application?
chunks.content:
What makes an enterprise web application different from a regular website?
A website primarily presents information or content. An enterprise web application supports authenticated users, business rules, data, transactions, workflows, integrations and role-based actions. The engineering focus therefore extends well beyond page design into architecture, security, data and operational reliability.
Can you modernise an existing application without rebuilding everything at once?
Yes. Where the existing system allows it, we can define APIs or service boundaries and introduce a modern web experience progressively. The right approach depends on the legacy architecture, business risk, integration constraints and which components genuinely need replacement.
Can the application integrate with our ERP, CRM or Microsoft 365 environment?
Yes, when the target platform provides suitable integration interfaces. We define data ownership, API contracts, identity, security and failure handling so the web application participates in the wider enterprise landscape without unnecessary duplication.
Which technology stack do you use for enterprise web applications?
Our core enterprise stack includes React for modern web experiences, ASP.NET/.NET for application and API services, and Microsoft SQL Server for structured business data, complemented by the most appropriate integration, cloud and reporting services for the requirement.
Do you support applications after go-live?
Yes. We can provide post-production support, issue resolution and planned enhancements, with the support model defined around application criticality, expected service needs and the agreed engagement scope.
