chunks.page_title: Mobile App Development | iOS & Android | Eureka Solutions
chunks.section_heading: Planning an iOS or Android application?
heading_path: Planning an iOS or Android application?
chunks.content:
Do you develop for both iOS and Android?
Yes. We can design mobile applications for both iOS and Android, with the implementation approach selected according to the product, device capabilities, integrations, performance expectations and long-term maintenance needs.
Do you use React Native or Flutter?
Both can be considered for cross-platform mobile delivery. We select the approach based on the application requirements, existing technology environment, device integrations, team and lifecycle considerations rather than treating one framework as the answer to every product.
Can the mobile app connect to our existing ERP, CRM or web application?
Yes, where suitable APIs or integration interfaces are available or can be created. We define secure service boundaries so the app can participate in existing business processes without connecting the device directly to backend databases or internal systems.
Can the app work when connectivity is poor?
Offline-aware behaviour can be designed where the business case requires it. The right solution depends on which data may be stored locally, what actions can occur offline, how conflicts should be handled and when synchronisation must happen.
Do you support app release and post-launch updates?
Yes. The engagement can include production release preparation, post-launch support, issue resolution and planned enhancements, with responsibilities and distribution requirements agreed for the specific application.

chunks.page_title: SaaS Product Development | MVP to Scale | Eureka Solutions

heading_path: Planning a new SaaS productâor productising an existing application?
chunks.content:
Can you help us build an MVP before investing in the full SaaS platform?
Yes. We can define an MVP around the smallest coherent set of capabilities needed to test the productâs value, while protecting architectural decisionsâsuch as identity, tenant context and data ownershipâthat could become expensive to reverse later.
Does every SaaS product need the same multi-tenant database model?
No. Tenant isolation can be implemented in different ways, and the correct pattern depends on security, scale, workload, customer requirements and operational constraints. We define the tenancy boundary first and choose the data and deployment model accordingly.
Can different customers have different product configurations?
Yes. SaaS products can support tenant-level configuration, feature availability and administrative settings where the product model requires them. We prefer controlled configuration over customer-specific code forks wherever practical.
Can subscription or billing services be integrated?
Yes, where the selected commercial and payment services provide suitable interfaces. We can model plans, entitlements or usage rules in the product and connect appropriate external billing capabilities according to the commercial requirement.
Can you help productise an existing custom application?
Yes. We first assess where the current application assumes a single customer, fixed configuration or deployment-specific behaviour, then identify the changes required for tenant awareness, reusable configuration, onboarding, administration, release management and operations.

Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.page_title: Self-Service Portal Development | Eureka Solutions
heading_path: Planning a self-service portal?
chunks.content:
How is a self-service portal different from a customer portal?
A customer portal is generally organised around the wider customer relationshipâaccount information, transactions, documents, service and engagement. A self-service portal is more specifically designed to let users find answers or complete defined services themselves. The two can overlap, and self-service capabilities are often part of a broader customer, employee or partner portal.
Can a self-service request automatically enter our internal workflow?
Yes, when appropriate interfaces or workflow services are available. We can connect submissions to business rules, APIs, workflow engines or enterprise systems so the request continues through the required process without unnecessary manual re-entry.
Can users see live request status?
Yes, where the underlying process exposes a reliable status. We define which system owns that status and how it is synchronised or retrieved so the portal presents a meaningful, current view to the user.
Can the portal support both authenticated and public services?
Potentially. Public information or low-risk services and authenticated account-specific services can be designed with different access boundaries. The correct model depends on the sensitivity of the data and action involved.
Can we launch with only a few services first?
Yes. A phased approach is often effective: establish the portal and identity foundation around a small set of high-value services, learn from real usage and then extend the catalogue and automation depth.
Which Repetitive Service Should Your Users Be Able to Handle Themselves?
